Former FTX Europe Head’s Perpetuals com Files to Trade Tokenized U.S. Stocks Under SEC Innovation Exemption Nasdaq-listed Perpetuals com, led by former FTX Europe head Patrick Gruhn, has filed with the SEC to operate a tokenized securities venue under the five-year Innovation Exemption. It is the second firm to pursue U.S. tokenized stock trading under the framework, after the OKX-ICE joint venture. Tokens must carry the same dividend and voting rights as ordinary shares, and companies have 30 days to object. Trading is planned via permissioned AMM pools on its Ethereum-compatible L2 Kronos X Public, with USDC as the settlement asset. A launch could come as early as mid-November. — link

September 2026 Exchange Derivatives Volume Report: total $3.84 trillion, MoM increased 9.4%, futures/spot ratio 5.51x WuBlockchain data show that derivatives trading volume across 12 major crypto exchanges reached $3.84 trillion in September 2026, up 9.4% from August. Binance led with $1.78 trillion (46.5% market share), followed by OKX at $698.8 billion (18.2%) and Bybit at $405.6 billion (10.6%). The top three exchanges accounted for 75.3% of total volume, up from 74.7% in August. Eight exchanges recorded monthly increases, while four saw declines. The futures-to-spot trading volume ratio fell to 5.51x from 6.87x, a 19.8% decrease. — link

Circle's USDC Becomes EU's First "Significant" E-Money Token Under MiCA The European Banking Authority (EBA) has classified Circle's USDC as the EU's first "significant" e-money token (EMT) under MiCA, making it the first of 45 notified EMTs to receive the designation. USDC is the world's second-largest stablecoin by market capitalization. Starting November 12, USDC will face joint supervision by the EBA and France's ACPR, with the EBA directly overseeing capital, reserves, liquidity, and recovery and redemption plans, while the ACPR retains oversight of governance and other operational matters. — link

BingX EU obtains Austria CASP license, to offer services across 29 EEA countries BingX EU (MEGE zweite GmbH) announced that it has obtained a Crypto-Asset Service Provider (CASP) license from Austria’s Financial Market Authority (FMA) under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). Subject to the completion of the relevant passporting arrangements, it will be able to offer regulated broker services across 29 countries in the European Economic Area, including crypto-asset custody, exchange and other crypto services. — link
